Subject: Post-call: Costing check-in and US vs EU residency impact (Finlytics)

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get a tailored pricing view for your internal finance review.

Call summary (TL;DR):
- Primary product: anomaly detection pipelines + real-time alert summaries (chat/completions + embeddings).
- Expected monthly active users (MAU): 250k with ~150M tokens/month current estimate (see attachment: finlytics_mau_projection.xlsx).
- Key ask: target cost guidance (target $/1M tokens) and visibility on US vs EU region unit delta due to residency.

Clarifying questions (please reply inline where helpful):
1) Token mix: roughly what percent of tokens are long-form generation vs short prompts/embeddings? We captured ~60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% misc in the deck — correct?
2) Residency requirement: Is EU residency required for all customer data, or only for EU-based end-customers?
3) Budget range: do you have a target monthly spend band for the pilot (e.g., $10k–$30k) vs projected steady-state?

Where we can help next:
- Karthik will produce a unit economics sketch showing target $/1M tokens at different batch/quantization configs and with/without EU residency premium.
- I can schedule a 30-min pricing deep-dive this week to walk Finance through assumptions.

Next steps I propose:
- Liam to confirm Q1–Q3 above by EOD Wed (Oct 7).
- Redwood to share initial $/1M token ranges (US and EU) and an estimated monthly bill for the pilot by Fri Oct 9.

Attachments: finlytics_mau_projection.xlsx (MAU/token assumptions).

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Post-call: Costing check-in and US vs EU residency impact (Finlytics)

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick answers then a question: 

1) Token mix: your breakdown is close. Updated split: 55% generation (long-form summaries), 35% embeddings, 10% prompts/metadata. Generation pieces skew long (avg 750 tokens) for batch summaries.
2) Residency: EU residency is required for EU customers' raw data only (we can route RU/US customers to US region), but Finlytics wants a single contract covering both regions. Important that billing visibility separates region costs.
3) Budget for pilot: Finance has signaled $15k–$25k/mo target for first 3 months; steady-state expectation TBD but could be 3x pilot if adoption ramps.

Question: can Redwood provide a modeled line item that shows per-1M token cost at three configurations:
  A) hosted US (default) with standard caching/batching
  B) hosted EU (data residency enforced) — show premium delta
  C) dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) assumption at 6mo vs on-demand

If we can get that by Friday that would help expedite procurement. Also include any assumptions about KV cache hit rates and effective tokenization differences (since summaries are long).

—Liam

Subject: Re: Post-call: Costing check-in and US vs EU residency impact (Finlytics)

Folks — quick pass on the numbers Liam asked for. Attached is a short PDF (redwood-eu-cost-breakdown.pdf) with the sketch; below is the executive summary. These are conservative starting assumptions; we can refine with real token traces.

Executive sketch (per 1M tokens):
- Config A — Hosted US (standard): $210 / 1M tokens (baseline)
  - Assumptions: 65% cache/batch efficiency, model variant: rw-large-v1, mixed-precision quantization nominal.
- Config B — Hosted EU (residency enabled): $260 / 1M tokens (approx +24% premium)
  - Drivers: EU GPU capacity premium, egress/networking, extra routing for regional isolation, KMS overheads.
- Config C — Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): $150 / 1M tokens (at 3-month ramp commit; unit drops with larger commit)
  - Notes: depends on commit size and burst handling; includes a separate SRE-managed pool, slightly lower per-token latency variance.

Additional notes:
- Long-form summaries (avg 750 tokens) have higher effective cost per user due to token length; effective $/1M for summary workload roughly +10–15% vs mixed-average if caching is low.
- Embeddings cost profile is significantly lower per logical unit, but you still pay per embedding compute and indexing storage; our spreadsheet maps embeddings to equivalent token-units for comparison.

I'll attach the PDF and can run a quick sensitivity with the numbers from finlytics_mau_projection.xlsx if you share a token trace.

Karthik

Perfect — thanks both. Liam, appreciate the clarified budget band. Two action items from Redwood: 

1) Karthik to produce a short sensitivity table (three rows: A/B/C configs) mapping to your pilot budget bands ($15k, $20k, $25k). Target delivery: Fri Oct 9 EOW.
2) Soojin to book a 30-min procurement + finance review for next Tue (Oct 13) 09:00–09:30 PT — invite coming.

If you can also share a small sample of token logs (redacted is fine) or confirm the monthly token projection sheet in the attachment, Karthik will include more precise cache-hit assumptions.

FYI — we'll mark EU residency as a routing/billing flag in the proposal so procurement can see separate line items; final contract language will reflect data residency SOW.

Thanks — sending calendar now.
